records.section_heading: Near-island biological hotspots in barren ocean basins
records.question: What percentage of coral reef ecosystems surveyed exhibited the Island Mass Effect (IME)?
records.ground_truth_answer: 91% of the coral reef ecosystems surveyed.
ground_truth_chunks: We show that IME is a near-ubiquitous feature among a majority (91%) of coral reef ecosystems surveyed, creating near-island 'hotspots' of phytoplankton biomass throughout the upper water column.

records.question: According to the Discussion, by how much could individual coral reef islands and atolls increase nearshore phytoplankton biomass over background oceanic conditions?
records.ground_truth_answer: Individual coral reef islands and atolls were capable of increasing the nearshore standing stock of phytoplankton biomass by up to 86% over background oceanic conditions.
ground_truth_chunks: Individual coral reef island and atolls were capable of increasing the nearshore standing stock of phytoplankton biomass by up to 86% over background oceanic conditions, forming biological hotspots across an otherwise barren ocean landscape.

records.question: Which predictors were included in the final best-specified GLM (model 1) for abs(b)?
records.ground_truth_answer: The best-specified model included Geomorphic Type, Reef Area, Bathymetric Slope, Population Status, and the interaction Reef Area: Geomorphic Type.
ground_truth_chunks: Following this iterative process, elevation, latitude, SST (mean and standard deviation) and the standard deviations of current speed and precipitation were removed. Remaining predictors were geomorphic type (atoll vs island), reef area, land area, bathymetric slope, population status (populated vs unpopulated), mean precipitation and mean current speed.

The resulting best-specified model was:

(1)  $abs(b) \sim Geomorphic Type + Reef Area + Bathymetric Slope + Population Status + Reef Area: Geomorphic Type$
